meta.source: International Monetary Fund, International Reserves and Foreign Currency Liquidity (IRFCL)

unitDetection.method: Each reporter's own USD figure divided by its own ounce figure gives an implied price per ounce, compared against the LBMA fix for the same month. A match at market or at the US statutory rate accepts the ounces as reported; a match only after dividing by a power of ten identifies a unit error.
unitDetection.referenceSeries: LBMA Gold Price PM, 14678 daily fixes

meta.indicatorNote: Gold (including gold deposits and, if appropriate, gold swapped), reported as volume in fine troy ounces and converted to tonnes at 31.1034768 g per troy ounce.
meta.valuationNote: Tonnes only. Every USD figure in this app is computed as tonnes x market price. The IMF USD columns are used to detect unit errors and to derive non-gold reserves, never to value gold: reporters carry gold at inconsistent valuations, the US at the statutory $42.2222/oz.
meta.shareNote: Gold's share of reserves is computed live as market-valued gold over (market-valued gold + non-gold reserves). Dividing the IMF's own gold USD by its own total would put US gold at 4 percent of reserves against a published figure of about 84 percent.
meta.coverageNote: Covers economies that report to the IMF reserves data template. Non-reporting holders are absent, as is gold held by the IMF and BIS themselves. Do not read the sum of these rows as a world total; cross-check against the World Gold Council.

scaleCorrections.evidence: This reporter's own dollar figure divided by its own ounce figure implies $4.0462 per ounce, 1000x below the market price. Dividing the volume by 1000 gives $4046.15 per ounce, a market price.
